payload.claim: `commit_squash` renders `outcome.attempts` into the permanent, pushed commit message ("N attempts, $X.XX"), but for a `RATE_LIMITED` outcome `CellOutcome.attempts` is never assigned in `saffron/cell/session.py`'s `except RateLimited` handler and silently keeps the dataclass default of 0. RATE_LIMITED-with-commits is one of the two scenarios this spec's own `Context` section cites as motivation ("A rate limit that landed during REBUT, after four commits and green gates"), so exactly that case will be pushed with a commit body reading "0 attempts, $19.17" or similar — internally inconsistent (nonzero spend, zero attempts) and understating the work captured on the branch, even though `spent_usd` for that same outcome is correctly read back via `ledger.task_spend`. Gates cannot see this because it is a plausible, well-formed commit message, not a crash or a lint violation.
